headline: Deinonychus and the Dinosaur Renaissance
subtitle: One Montana theropod, one landmark monograph and a change in how dinosaurs were imagined.
standfirst: Deinonychus antirrhopus is a small-ish predatory dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous of western North America. Its importance is not that it was the first active dinosaur, or the first bird-like one. It is that a detailed skeleton gave researchers a new anatomical case to argue from.

blocks.title: A quarry, a monograph, a change in emphasis.

paragraphs: Barnum Brown collected fragmentary remains in southern Montana in 1931, but the material was not described as a new genus. From 1964 onward, John Ostrom’s Yale Peabody Museum expeditions recovered multiple individuals from the Cloverly Formation. Ostrom named Deinonychus antirrhopus in 1969. [[ostrom1969]]

The type specimen, YPM 5205, is not a complete animal. It is a collection of bones with a history: quarry, excavation, preparation, comparison and publication. Its significance was built through that work, not discovered whole in the ground. [[ostrom1969]]

blocks.note: The holotype of Deinonychus antirrhopus, and the subject of Ostrom’s 1969 monograph.

blocks.title: The anatomy of an active animal.

paragraphs: Ostrom’s monograph described a theropod with a lightly built skull, grasping hands and an enlarged second pedal claw. He argued that the animal’s anatomy was consistent with an active, bird-like creature rather than a slow, sprawling reptile. [[ostrom1969]]

The argument did not rest on the sickle claw alone. It drew on the whole skeleton: the proportions of the limbs, the structure of the hip and the bird-like features of the hand and foot. The monograph gave a broad anatomical case that later researchers could test, extend or dispute. [[ostrom1969]][[fowler2011]]

blocks.title: A fossil is not a behaviour
blocks.body: A joint can constrain movement. A claw can suggest a function. Neither can record what an animal did on a particular afternoon. Behaviour has to be inferred from anatomy, trace fossils, associations and comparison with living animals — and each of those lines has limits.

paragraphs: The phrase Dinosaur Renaissance describes a broader mid-twentieth-century reassessment of dinosaur activity, growth and relationship to birds. Ostrom’s work became a touchstone for that shift, but it was not the sole cause of it. The change came through many researchers, specimens and arguments, not one heroic discovery. [[ostrom1969]]

The important shift was methodological as well as imaginative. Dinosaurs were increasingly treated as animals whose anatomy could be compared with living birds and crocodilians, rather than as symbols of a failed evolutionary experiment.

blocks.title: What changed in the reading of the animal

left.label: A common older image
left.title: Slow, cold and sprawling
left.body: A popular mid-century image treated large dinosaurs as sluggish reptiles, with posture and behaviour modelled on crocodiles or lizards. It was an image, not a single scientific consensus.
points: Behaviour inferred from a narrow modern analogue

right.label: The anatomical case
right.title: Active, bird-related, arguable
right.body: Ostrom’s description made the bird-like details of the skeleton part of a detailed functional argument. It did not prove a single metabolic rate or behaviour, but it changed the questions researchers could ask.
points: Physiology and behaviour opened to testing

blocks.note: The contrast is a history of interpretations, not a scoreboard. Older researchers were not uniformly wrong, and newer reconstructions are not automatically right.

paragraphs: Multiple Deinonychus individuals have been found associated with the larger herbivorous dinosaur Tenontosaurus. Ostrom and later authors considered cooperative hunting a plausible explanation for the association. A plausible explanation is not the same as a documented behaviour. [[maxwell1995]]

Roach and Brinkman reviewed the evidence for gregariousness and cooperative pack hunting in Deinonychus and other non-avian theropods. They cautioned that a bonebed association does not demonstrate a coordinated pack. Scavenging, a predator trap, a drought accumulation or independent individuals drawn to a carcass could produce a similar pattern. [[roach2007]]

blocks.title: What the assemblage can say
blocks.body: The association is real. The behaviour behind it is not uniquely determined. Cooperative hunting remains a hypothesis, not a fact to be repeated because it makes a better illustration.

paragraphs: Deinonychus is not Velociraptor. They are different genera, separated by geography and time, even though both are dromaeosaurids. The popular confusion says more about the reach of a film franchise than about the fossil record. [[turner2007]]

The wider importance of Deinonychus lies in the connection it helped make visible: the same anatomical tradition that produced birds also produced non-flying predatory dinosaurs. Feathers are part of that story, but they are not a single answer to every question about the animal. [[ostrom1969]][[xu2014]]

blocks.label: The argument
blocks.text: One good skeleton can change a question without answering it.
